pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Change the glTF loader to use `Camera3dBundle`
pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #7889.

## Solution

- Change the glTF loader to insert a `Camera3dBundle` instead of a manually constructed bundle. This might prevent future issues when new components are required for a 3D Camera to work correctly.
- Register the `ColorGrading` type because `bevy_scene` was complaining about it.

issue_context.title: `scene_viewer` crashes when running a gltf that includes a camera.
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version

Bevy main 47ddd4a8ce98b20ce14b67f6579b1c201a08bc77

## What you did

Run the `scene_viewer` example with a gltf that includes a camera (exporting the default blender scene and make sure to check Include->Cameras when exporting works)

## What went wrong

It crashes.

## Additional information

```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at 'called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: QueryDoesNotMatch(6039v0)', D:\programming\bevy\crates\bevy_render\src\render_phase\draw.rs:268:54
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
thread 'Compute Task Pool (7)' panicked at 'A system has panicked so the executor cannot continue.: RecvError', crates\bevy_ecs\src\schedule\executor\multi_threaded.rs:194:60
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at 'called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value', D:\programming\bevy\crates\bevy_tasks\src\task_pool.rs:376:49
thread 'Compute Task Pool (7)' panicked at 'called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: RecvError', crates\bevy_render\src\pipelined_rendering.rs:136:45
thread 'main' panicked at 'called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value', D:\programming\bevy\crates\bevy_tasks\src\task_pool.rs:376:49
```
comments: I would have bet it was related to my changes with the prepass shader for shadows thing, but a git bisect led to this commit being the cause: 912fb5886908373db2b7c0140ae15961ccd92f72. I will look into it.

Ok, found the issue: The problem is that the gltf loader does not create a `Camera3dBundle` which would have included the new `Tonemapping` component. Because it is missing the view query in `queue_mesh_view_bind_groups` does not include the camera and does not insert the required `MeshViewBindGroup` component which later results in the `QueryDoesNotMatch` error inside `draw`.

I will open a PR fixing this.

review_comments: What's the purpose of Transform -> Matrix -> Transform?

Those are two different Transform types: one is the bevy Transform type and the other is the glTF specific transform type. I just extracted the bevy Transform into a local variable because I need it again for the Camera3dBundle if the node is a camera.

Does setting the camera's transform here make sense when you've already set the parent node to the same transform?

The results look correct, but IMO it feels wrong.

It's not the parent node that has the same transform, it's the camera node itself. The `Camera3dBundle` is inserted after the `SpatialBundle`, and because both have a `Transform` component, the camera bundle overwrites the transform of the spatial bundle. So we use the same transform twice.

It feels wrong, but there aren't currently a way to add a "partial" bundle. The other way to fix this would be to add manually the component of the bundle specific to the camera, but then it will crash again next time we add a new mandatory component for cameras.
